en: Post-storm Highveld air should be bottled and sold overseas.
af: Die Hooglandlug ná reën behoort in 'n botteltjie verkoop te word.
flag_reason: `embodleleni` is attested as an Ndebele/siSwati-type form, not standard isiZulu `ebhodleleni`.

en: Somebody's mom is going to have words. Worth it.
af: Iemand se ma gaan iets sê. Dit was die moeite werd.
flag_reason: `Kufanele` means it is necessary/should be so; it does not convey the punchline that the trouble was worth it.

en: The sun is buffering. Do not refresh the page.
af: Die son buffer nog. Moenie die bladsy verfris nie.
flag_reason: `-bafura` is an unattested coined-looking adaptation of English `buffer`, despite the draft's HIGH confidence.

en: No colours in the sky tonight, just shades of calm.
af: Geen kleure in die lug vanaand nie, net skakerings van rustig.
flag_reason: `izigaba` means stages/levels, not shades, so the visual image of shades of calm is lost.

en: The evening is tiptoeing in on socks.
af: Die aand kom binne op sokkies.
flag_reason: The line says the evening enters on foot wearing socks; it drops the specific tiptoe action.

en: Tomorrow is a fresh negotiation with the weather. Tonight we rest.
af: Môre is 'n nuwe onderhandeling met die weer. Vanaand rus ons.
flag_reason: `ingxoxo` is a conversation/discussion, not the negotiation named by the English joke.

en: Clouds today, vibes optional.
af: Windgat wolke vandag.
flag_reason: The draft says today's clouds are sulking; it drops the English idea that the vibes are optional.

en: Cape Town sends solidarity. And a spare cap.
af: Kaapstad stuur sterkte. En 'n ekstra pet.
flag_reason: `ukubambisana` is cooperation rather than solidarity, and `elilodwa eliphelele` is one complete cap rather than a spare cap.

en: The South-Easter has no off switch. We've looked.
af: Die Suidoos het nie 'n af-knoppie nie. Ons het gesoek.
flag_reason: `Sesikhangile` could not be attested as the isiZulu wording for `we have looked/searched` and resembles a cross-Nguni near-match.

en: The tablecloth is pressed and ready for tomorrow's service.
af: Die tafeldoek is gestryk en reg vir môre se diens.
flag_reason: `indwangu iyashisiwe` says the cloth is heated/burned, not pressed or ironed.

en: Prettiest blue sky in the country, and it feels like a fridge with a view.
af: Mooiste blou lug in die land, en dit voel soos 'n yskas met uitsig.
flag_reason: `enombukiso` means with a show/display, not with a view, so the fridge-with-a-view image fails.

en: Winter sun: all of the light, none of the heat. Nice try, sun.
af: Winterson: al die lig, nul van die hitte. Mooi probeer, son.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: Trout weather. Lovely for the fish. Character-building for the fisherman.
af: Forelweer. Vir die vis is dit lekker. Vir die visserman is dit karakterbou.
flag_reason: `Sihle kuyo inhlanzi` has a malformed agreement/locative frame for `lovely for the fish`.

en: The blesbok wear no scarves and file no complaints. We could learn something. We won't, but we could.
af: Die blesbokke dra nie serpe nie en kla ook nie. Ons kan iets leer. Ons gaan nie, maar ons kan.
flag_reason: The specific blesbok is reduced to generic antelope/game, breaking the animal-specific comparison.

en: Forgot to switch the electric blanket on in advance. Every. Single. Night.
af: Elektriese kombers weer vergeet om vooraf aan te sit. Elke. Enkele. Aand.
flag_reason: `Bonke. Ubusuku. Bonke.` uses plural-person concords around singular `ubusuku` and does not form `every single night`.

en: That one little light is someone doing winter correctly: hut, fire, done.
af: Daardie een liggie is iemand wat winter reg doen: hut, vuur, klaar.
flag_reason: `bani` means `who`; `Lelo bani elilodwa elincane` does not denote the one little light.

en: The front left. The cold just moved in permanently.
af: Die front is weg. Die koue het net getrek, nie geloop nie.
flag_reason: `isiphepho` is a storm, not the cold/weather front required by the line.

en: The 7am sun isn't giving heat yet. Only vibes.
af: Sewe-uur se son deel nog nie hitte uit nie, net vibes.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: The sun is doing admin out here. Heat was not part of the package.
af: Die son doen sy admin buite. Hitte is nie deel van die pakket nie.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: Cape Town after a front: clean, bright, and honestly freezing.
af: Kaapstad ná 'n front: skoon, helder, en yskoud eerlik.
flag_reason: `isiphepho` is a storm, not the cold/weather front required by the line.

en: Mzansi winter does colour like nobody else. Warmth, though...
af: Winter in Mzansi doen kleur soos niemand anders nie.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: One blanket, two people, zero shame.
af: Een kombers, twee mense, geen skaamte nie.
flag_reason: `awukho amahloni` has singular concord with plural `amahloni`; the negative agreement is malformed.

en: The Karoo is opening its roof for the night. Dress warm for the show.
af: Die Karoo maak nou die dak oop. Trek warm aan vir die vertoning.
flag_reason: `Gqoka okufudumele umbukiso` omits the relation meaning `for the show` and is not a complete construction.

en: The moon switched the mountains on. The heat, however, stays off.
af: Die maan het die berge aangeskakel. Die hitte, egter, nie.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: The sea is 12 degrees. By ten o'clock it's going to feel like a spa.
af: Die see is 12 grade. Teen tienuur gaan dit soos 'n spa voel.
flag_reason: `Ulwandle luma-degree ayi-12` fuses/misforms the possession construction and reads as though the sea bites a degree.

en: We don't talk about today. Today is over. We're proud of us.
af: Ons praat nie oor vandag nie. Vandag is verby. Ons is trots op ons.
flag_reason: `Namuhla luphelile` assigns a noun-class concord to the adverb `namuhla`; the clause is malformed.

en: The rocks will be handing out today's heat all night. Free of charge.
af: Die klippe gaan vannag nog die dag se hitte uitdeel. Verniet.
flag_reason: `ushisa` is an inflected verb form used as though it were the noun `heat/warmth`; the nominal form is malformed.

en: The whole city had the same plan tonight. Look at us all.
af: Die hele stad het vanaand dieselfde plan gehad. Kyk hoe lyk ons.
flag_reason: `Bheka sonke` does not encode `look at all of us`; the object/concord needed for `us` is missing.

en: The sprinkler is supposedly for the lawn. Look who's all standing in the water.
af: Die sproeier is kamma vir die gras. Kyk wie staan almal in die water.
flag_reason: `Bheka ukuthi bonke abamile emanzini ngobani` is a malformed interrogative and does not cleanly say `look who is standing in the water`.

en: Relax, the mountains are just buffering.
af: Moenie stres nie — die berge buffer nog.
flag_reason: `-bafura` is an unattested coined-looking adaptation of English `buffer`, despite the draft's HIGH confidence.

en: Every window switching on is someone deciding: that's enough for today.
af: Elke venster wat aangaan is iemand wat besluit het: genoeg vir vandag.
flag_reason: `ifasitela elivulayo` is a window opening, not a window/light switching on.

en: Perfect weather to bump into someone you've 'been meaning to call'.
af: Perfekte weer om iemand raak te loop wat jy 'nog wou bel'.
flag_reason: `obu-'uhlose` has a broken fused quote/relative construction and is not valid morphology.

en: Every glow down there is someone else who also can't believe it's already winter.
af: Elke liggie daar onder is iemand wat ook nie kan glo dis al winter nie.
flag_reason: `ongakholwa nokukholwa` duplicates incompatible forms and leaves the clause malformed.

en: The foghorn is Sea Point's free white-noise machine.
af: Die mishoring is Seepunt se gratis witgeraas-masjien.
flag_reason: `i-foghorn iyimishini` gives a singular horn a plural/mass `machines/machinery` complement.

en: The sun took its time this morning. Worth the wait.
af: Die son vat sy tyd vanoggend, en dit wys.
flag_reason: `Kufanele ukulinda` says one should wait, not that the result was worth the wait.

en: Days like this aren't earned. They're issued.
af: Só 'n dag koop jy nie. Jy kry hom net.
flag_reason: `aziholelwa` means the days are not paid/salaried, not that they are not earned.

en: The sun is really milking this exit. Honestly, deserved.
af: Die son gaan af soos hy weet ons kyk.
flag_reason: `umphumo` is an outcome/result, not the sun's exit; the core `milking this exit` joke no longer parses.

en: Golden hour runs daily. Attendance still somehow optional.
af: Goue uur: elke dag gratis, en ons is elke dag weer verbaas.
flag_reason: `Ukuza kwayo` makes the golden hour's arrival optional, whereas the English says the audience's attendance is optional.
